items.title: A credit-balance 400 is not the usage-limit wall, and every run pays for that.
items.detail: 2026-08-23: all three crons died with `Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API` and exited 1, so the day went red and the episode only shipped from a manual dispatch at 14:42 UTC, six hours late. `_usage_limit_reset` keys on the string `usage limit`, which this message does not contain, so `check_api_budget()` printed "preflight inconclusive — continuing" and the run went on to spend 40 article body fetches, ~37 Brave enrichment calls and an agentic research call before failing at the script call — three times over, which is the exact waste the preflight was written to prevent (see its docstring on 2026-07-25). Match the credit-balance refusal too and exit `EXIT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`; the workflow already turns 75 into a skipped day with a warning instead of a failure.

items.title: The review goes quiet on exactly the days worth reviewing.
items.detail: `main()` only fetches a job log from a run whose conclusion is `success`. On 2026-08-23 there was no such run, so the review published a bare trigger table and no narrative — three failures and not a word about why. Fall back to the newest failed run's log (the facts are all there: the 400 above is in it), and keep the successful-run preference for ordinary days.

items.title: The review cannot see the run that made the episode when a cron did not.
items.detail: It is gated on the third cron, so 2026-08-23's manual dispatch four hours later is absent from the write-up and from the archive. Either widen `fetch_runs` past `event: schedule` for the day, or make the review re-runnable for a date and re-publish over the same file (`--date` already exists; the index and feed update in place).

items.title: The review reports itself as an unfinished run.
items.detail: The `review` job runs inside the 3:05 AM cron's own workflow run, so every review to date ends with "Fallback 2 … in_progress" and the narrative reads it as a pending unknown ("a third in progress at review time", 2026-08-20). `summarize_runs` knows `GITHUB_RUN_ID`; label that row as the reviewing run so the model stops treating it as a cliffhanger.

items.title: Decide what to do about scheduler drift.
items.detail: Every trigger in the sample started late: +44/+29/+32 (08-20), +46/+31/+31 (08-21), +34/+20/+25 (08-22), +35/+22/+25 (08-23). This is GitHub's scheduled-run queue, not the pipeline, and the reviews report it as a fault every single day. Either move the crons earlier and accept the drift as the schedule, or keep the number and stop framing it as one — a fact reported daily as a problem and never acted on trains the reader to skip the paragraph.

items.title: Watch the four 2026-08-22 fixes on air.
items.detail: None has been observed in a shipped episode: the runs the day after all died at the credit wall. The first green day's review is the check — citation alignment should land near 51%/55% rather than 5-8/15 and 0-1/deep dive, `tts_short_segments` should be ~2% of segments rather than 13 of 16, and the canary should only pin OpenAI after two timeouts per model.

items.title: Gemini has not rendered an episode in the review window.
items.detail: 08-20, 08-21 and 08-22 all pinned OpenAI on canary read timeouts against `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`; 08-23 never got that far. The probe item under Short-term is the diagnostic — the reviews now give it a daily before/after record, so run it and read the next week's reviews rather than re-reasoning about the ladder.

items.title: All three scheduled triggers failed or did not complete on August 26th.
items.detail: The primary run (08:54 UTC) and Fallback 1 (09:40 UTC) both concluded in failure. Fallback 2 (10:40 UTC) was still in progress at the last update (10:44 UTC), meaning no episode was produced for the day. Three consecutive attempts to execute the pipeline all either failed or remained unfinished, which suggests a systematic problem rather than transient flakiness. Check the run logs at https://github.com/zirnhelt/curated-podcast-generator/actions/runs/32950154292 and https://github.com/zirnhelt/curated-podcast-generator/actions/runs/32954282339 to identify the failure mode that struck both the primary and first fallback identically.

items.title: Gemini TTS rate limit (HTTP 429) triggered twice on canary checks, forcing full OpenAI render.
items.detail: On 2026-08-27, the Gemini TTS pre-flight check failed with HTTP 429 errors on two separate canary attempts. The pipeline's fallback logic caught both failures before audio synthesis began and switched the entire episode to OpenAI rather than risk a mid-episode voice change. The mechanism is clear: Gemini's quota was exhausted before the render stage. To close this, either increase the Gemini quota tier for the API key, implement request queuing to respect rate limits, or add a secondary Gemini endpoint (via Vertex AI) as a separate capacity pool.

items.title: Roundup story order drifted again despite a repair pass, with 3 of 15 stories airing out of sequence.
items.detail: On 2026-08-27, the script/roundup-order segment failed once, was repaired, and still shipped with 3 stories in the wrong position relative to their assigned blocks. Of 15 roundup citations total, 13 matched their sources, but the 3 misaligned stories suggest the repair pass did not fully resolve the ordering logic. The deep dive citations fared worse: 0 of 3 matched. The root cause is in the roundup ordering algorithm—either it does not persist constraints across repair cycles, or the repair itself reintroduces drift. Trace the sort order during and after the repair pass to identify whether the issue is in the initial sort, the repair logic, or both.

items.title: Brave Answers API hit its usage limit partway through the run, forcing a fallback to web snippets.
items.detail: On 2026-08-27, the script/brave-answers segment failed with HTTP 402 (usage limit exceeded) after the quota was exhausted. The pipeline switched to web snippets for all remaining answers in that episode. The 402 error itself indicates the account hit its hard limit, not a transient failure. Confirm the quota tier on the Brave account, assess whether the episode's answer count is typical, and decide whether to increase the quota, implement batching, or rely on web snippets as the primary source when the API is unavailable.

items.title: One TTS segment returned audio shorter than its word count predicts, requiring a retry.
items.detail: On 2026-08-27, one text-to-speech take produced audio duration shorter than the word count would estimate. The pipeline retried once per protocol and the issue resolved. This is a single occurrence and may be transient voice synthesis variance. If this recurs across multiple segments or runs, it signals either a systematic issue in duration estimation, a problem with a particular voice model, or the TTS API's handling of edge-case text. Monitor for recurrence; if it persists, audit the duration formula against actual TTS output and consider adding a tolerance band before flagging a retry.

items.title: Gemini multi-speaker TTS timed out on the welcome section, forcing a mid-episode fallback to OpenAI.
items.detail: During audio render on 2026-08-28, the welcome section synthesis via Gemini multi-speaker hit a ReadTimeout after 120 seconds on generativelanguage.googleapis.com. The pipeline fell back to OpenAI for that section and all remaining sections and credits. The episode now spans two TTS providers—Gemini for welcome, OpenAI for body and outro—introducing a voice discontinuity in the shipped 17.7-minute episode. Investigate whether Gemini's multi-speaker quota or concurrency limits are being hit, and consider either increasing timeouts, implementing section-level retry logic before switching providers, or pre-allocating Gemini synthesis for critical segments at off-peak times.

items.title: Ten roundup stories remained out of sequence after one correction pass.
items.detail: On 2026-08-29, the script/roundup-order segment failed to sort correctly on the first attempt. After one repair pass, 10 stories still aired after a later block. The pipeline did not retry. This follows the pattern noted in the already-tracked item roundup-citation-alignment-drift-persists, where 3 of 15 stories drifted out of order on a prior run. The repair logic is insufficient; either increase retry attempts on sort failures or add a validation gate that blocks publish if any story lands in the wrong temporal position.

items.title: Gemini project spend cap was reached mid-run, forcing a fallback to OpenAI for the entire episode's text-to-speech.
items.detail: On 2026-08-30, the render/gemini-canary segment degraded because the Gemini project spend cap had been reached. The pipeline fell back to OpenAI rather than risk a mid-episode voice change, rendering all 22.6 minutes on a different provider. The Gemini pre-flight check also failed to answer, removing any option to recover partway through. Raising the spend cap or implementing a per-segment budget ceiling that triggers earlier would prevent this fallback and keep rendering consistent.

items.title: Gemini multi-speaker TTS has timed out three times in two days, forcing provider fallback mid-episode.
items.detail: On 2026-09-01, the news section hit a 120-second read timeout on Gemini's generativelanguage.googleapis.com endpoint during multi-speaker synthesis. Two canary checks against the same model failed at 45 seconds earlier that morning. The pipeline fell back to OpenAI for the remaining sections and credits, creating an audible voice delivery inconsistency (Casey-to-Riley ratio 0.68 across the whole episode but synthesized on different providers for different segments). Check whether Gemini's multi-speaker quota or rate limit is exhausted, confirm the project's tier and spend cap status via the Gemini console, and either increase the timeout threshold with exponential backoff for retries, or switch multi-speaker sections to OpenAI by default if Gemini's quota is not recoverable.

items.title: Gemini multi-speaker TTS rejected the preamble section with no audio output.
items.detail: On 2026-09-03 at 09:05, Gemini's multi-speaker model returned a finish reason of OTHER for the preamble with zero audio despite accepting the prompt. Four single-speaker attempts followed, all rejecting or returning silence. The pipeline fell back to OpenAI for remaining sections and credits, splitting the episode's voice mid-section rather than dropping content. Determine whether the preamble text shape triggers a known Gemini limitation, whether the quota tier has multi-speaker restrictions, or whether this is transient flakiness requiring only a retry budget increase.

items.title: Fallback 2 scheduled trigger started 291 minutes late and remains in-progress.
items.detail: On 2026-09-03 at 14:56 UTC, the 3:05 AM Pacific fallback trigger (scheduled for ~11:05 UTC) started 291 minutes late and was still in-progress when the review ran. Three manual runs occurred before the scheduled time, and the facts do not explain why the fallback ran so late or why it stalled. Check the GitHub Actions scheduler logs and the in-progress run URL https://github.com/zirnhelt/curated-podcast-generator/actions/runs/33769783188 to determine whether the runner is hung, whether there is a capacity bottleneck, or whether the cron expression is misconfigured.

items.title: Casey's speaking time exceeds Riley's by 13 percent.
items.detail: The voice_ratio_casey_over_riley measured 1.13 on 2026-09-04. No target range is defined in the config, so it is unclear whether this represents acceptable variance or systematic drift. Establish a target voice ratio (e.g., 1.0 or 1.05) in the episode config and add a quality check that flags ratios outside a defined band. If this ratio persists across future runs, adjust the host distribution weights in the synthesis prompt.

items.title: Gemini multi-speaker TTS timed out on the deep-dive section after five attempts.
items.detail: On 2026-09-06, the deep-dive section timed out on `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` multi-speaker mode after 5 unanswered attempts (ReadTimeout: HTTPSConnectionPool, read timeout=88). The pipeline fell back to OpenAI for that section and all credits, creating a mid-episode voice discontinuity. Listeners heard Gemini's voice on the roundup, OpenAI on deep dives and credits. This is the third Gemini multi-speaker timeout in the tracked issues. Implement exponential backoff with a per-section timeout ceiling, or switch multi-speaker sections to single-speaker Gemini rendering when multi-speaker fails, to avoid provider fragmentation mid-episode.

items.title: The daily anchor framing received no per-weekday variations in the prompt.
items.detail: On 2026-09-07, the debate question 'When storytelling tools become easier to use, what institutional knowledge and editorial judgment disappears along with the difficulty, and how do newsrooms maintain that skill?' was framed unaided each day without structural diversity. Add a weekday-specific framing layer to the anchor prompt—examples, angles, or constraints that vary Monday through Friday—so listeners hear evolution across the week rather than repetition.

items.title: Brave body-backfill budget exhaustion is recurring and requires intervention.
items.detail: On 2026-09-08, the pipeline spent its full 12-call Brave budget during script generation, forcing nine articles to ship with stub bodies instead of full text. The degradations log lists this same reason 12 times. This pattern matches the 2026-09-02 incident (tracked as brave-body-budget-hit-55-article-drop) where 55 articles were dropped. The mechanism is a fixed call budget that does not reset between runs or scale with article volume. To close this: either expand the Brave quota in config, implement per-article fallback logic that drops sparse articles before scripting rather than airing them, or track Brave spend across runs and alert when 80% of the budget is consumed.

items.title: Gemini multi-speaker TTS failed on the news section with HTTP 500, requiring fallback to single-speaker.
items.detail: On 2026-09-08, the Gemini multi-speaker model failed on the news section with an HTTP 500 error. The pipeline retried and succeeded using Gemini single-speaker on retry 1. Two other sections later synthesized on the same retry, so their delivery may differ from the rest of the episode. The error message is truncated (RuntimeError: Gemini TTS HTTP 500: {) and the root cause is not available. To close this: log the full Gemini response body on 5xx errors, check whether the news section's character count or speaker boundary exceeds Gemini multi-speaker's limits, and consider raising the retry budget for TTS or splitting large sections at speaker boundaries before sending to Gemini.

items.title: Two Gemini-rendered sections shipped with degraded context after failing on earlier retry attempts.
items.detail: On 2026-09-09, one section synthesized on retry 3 with context and style information dropped, and another on retry 2 with context dropped. Both shipped in the final episode with potential delivery variance from the rest of the content. The pipeline does not track which sections these are or expose their identity in the degradations log, making it impossible to audit whether listeners noticed the deviation or to improve the retry strategy.

items.title: Three instances of AI-tell language patterns passed quality checks and shipped in the final episode.
items.detail: On 2026-09-09, the quality check detected 3 AI-tell pattern hits in the shipped script. These phrases remained in the audio and RSS feed. The detection system is working, but the pipeline has no gate to reject episodes with pattern hits or halt publication for manual review before shipping.

items.title: Manual dispatch and fallback trigger both launched but neither finished by review time.
items.detail: On 2026-09-10, run 34488334052 started at 14:19:51Z via manual dispatch and remained in_progress. Run 34492356898 started at 14:56:26Z under Fallback 2 (3:05 AM Pacific trigger) and remained pending. Both runs fell significantly behind schedule: the manual run was 254 minutes late, and the fallback run was 291 minutes late despite starting 37 minutes after the first. The pending state of the second run suggests it may be blocked waiting for the first to complete. Determine whether Fallback 2 should wait for manual runs or execute independently, and add monitoring to alert when either run stalls beyond a threshold (for example, in_progress for more than 2 hours).

items.title: Gemini TTS HTTP 403 on canary forces full episode render on OpenAI.
items.detail: Both gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts and gemini-2.5-flash-tts returned HTTP 403 on the pre-flight check on 2026-09-12. The pipeline bypassed Gemini entirely and rendered all 19 minutes of audio on OpenAI instead of attempting retry or section-level fallback. The episode shipped on time with no audio missing. Determine whether the 403 is a quota issue, a permissions issue, or a service degradation. If it recurs, the canary should log the error detail before fallback so the next incident response is faster.

items.title: Deep dive citations matched at 33% versus roundup at 80%.
items.detail: On September 13, the roundup section matched 12 of 15 citations (80%), but the deep dive section matched only 1 of 3 (33%). The gap suggests a different verification pathway or a shortfall in source retrieval for longer-form segments. The debate question on Roberts Bank Terminal 2 proceeded despite this disparity. Audit the deep dive citation matching logic and the Brave API call sequence to confirm whether thin article bodies or budget exhaustion degraded the deep dive's source alignment.

items.title: Forty-three roundup stories were dropped entirely before scripting.
items.detail: The pipeline dropped 43 roundup articles outright, far exceeding normal story filtering. This happened upstream of the citation alignment check (which only saw 15 roundup sources total). Combined with the Brave body-backfill budget exhaustion flagged five times in degradations, the pipeline appears to have culled heavily to stay within cost constraints. To close this: log the drop reason for each culled article and set a threshold alert when drops exceed a baseline percentage of the incoming feed.

items.title: Daily anchor framing applied the same debate question without per-weekday context.
items.detail: The debate question—"Who decides what stories get told and preserved in local communities, and how can digital tools democratize both the creation and archiving of cultural memory?"—was used identically across all days on 2026-09-14, with no per-weekday customization in the prompt or template. The degradation log notes "no per-weekday framings" and "each day frames the question unaided." To close this: add branching logic to the anchor framing stage that seeds the prompt with day-of-week context or topic hints, similar to how other segments vary by publication date.

items.title: Script expansion closed only 3 percent of the gap to the target word count.
items.detail: On 2026-09-17, the first draft arrived at 2,802 words against a 3,400-word target, triggering an expand pass. The shipped script landed at 2,896 words—a gain of 94 words when 598 were needed to reach target. This is the second consecutive run where expansion fell far short: on 2026-09-16, expansion produced a final count 426 words below target. The mechanism suggests the expansion prompt or its iteration limit is not aggressive enough to close multi-hundred-word gaps. Investigate whether the expansion pass has a word-growth ceiling, whether it runs for a fixed iteration count rather than until target is met, or whether the LLM is rejecting longer rewrites. Match the target validation logic so expansion runs until the shipped script reaches the goal.

items.title: Forty-five roundup articles were dropped with no logged reason.
items.detail: The episode included 3 deep dives but dropped 45 roundup articles, resulting in 233 total RSS episodes shipped. The degradation log cites Brave body-backfill budget exhaustion (12 calls spent) as the cause of thin article stubs, but does not state whether those 45 articles were culled before scripting, after citation work, or during final assembly. The review infers the drops were architectural rather than accidental because the pipeline completed successfully, but the facts do not confirm this. Add explicit logging at each stage that removes articles—sourcing, body backfill, citation matching, and final script assembly—so the next run's review can trace which step and which count of articles caused the drop.

items.title: One object referenced in the podcast feed is missing from R2 storage and will cause 404 errors.
items.detail: On September 22, a single file present in podcast-feed.xml could not be found in R2 and could not be rebuilt from disk. The pipeline completed and published successfully despite this mismatch, leaving crawlers to encounter a 404 when following the RSS reference. Identify which object is missing, restore it to R2, or remove the reference from the feed XML before the next publish cycle.

items.title: Two sentences with unsupported Indigenous nation references remained in the script after territory-check rewrites failed.
items.detail: On September 22, the territory-check system flagged two sentences claiming Tsilhqot'in nation in contexts the territory map covers as other nations. The system attempted rewrites and rejected them. The two sentences shipped in the final episode anyway, carrying geographic claims the validation layer could not support. Log which sentences triggered the rewrite rejection, and decide whether to cut them, override the territory map data, or implement a mandatory-cut rule when rewrites fail.
